stem: Which port does Modbus/TCP use?
explanation: Classic Modbus/TCP listens on 502 with no authentication or encryption; the TLS-secured variant uses 802.
optionNotes: 20000 is DNP3.
44818 is EtherNet/IP explicit messaging.
102 is Siemens S7comm over ISO-TSAP.
Correct: IANA mbap.

stem: Which protocol is most associated with electric and water utility telemetry between a master and outstations?
explanation: DNP3 is widely used in the electric and water sectors; its Secure Authentication extension adds challenge-response.
optionNotes: MQTT is an IoT pub/sub protocol.
Correct: DNP3 (IEEE 1815), port 20000.
CoAP is a constrained IoT REST protocol.
Zigbee is a short-range IoT mesh radio.

stem: Why is the classic Modbus protocol considered risky when a controller is reachable from an untrusted network?
options: It has no authentication or encryption, so any reachable client can read or write registers
It uses a weak cipher that is easily broken
It requires a password that is emailed in the clear
explanation: Modbus was built for trusted networks. Segmentation and allowlists, not the protocol, provide the security.
optionNotes: Correct.
Classic Modbus has no cipher at all, not a weak one.
It runs over TCP or serial.
There is no built-in password mechanism.

stem: An operator's HMI keeps showing normal tank levels while the physical process is actually overflowing, because the controller reports were altered. Which ATT&CK for ICS effect is this?
explanation: Manipulation of View feeds operators false data. Cross-check with independent instruments and out-of-band monitoring.
optionNotes: Denial of Control is being unable to send commands.
Loss of Availability is losing the process or system, not a false reading.
Correct: the operator's view is falsified.
Damage to Property is the physical result, not the false display.

stem: What is the primary job of a safety instrumented system (SIS)?
options: Route business email to the plant
Bring the process to a safe state when limits are exceeded
explanation: An SIS is independent of normal control and trips the process to a safe state. Triton targeted an SIS.
optionNotes: That is IT infrastructure, unrelated to safety.
Correct.
That is an HMI.
That is a data historian.

stem: A worm reaches an isolated control network on a USB drive, then changes the speed commands sent to variable-frequency drives while hiding the change from the engineering software. Which historical incident does this match?
explanation: Stuxnet crossed an air gap on removable media, altered drive parameters and used a rootkit to hide PLC changes.
optionNotes: Correct: Stuxnet targeted Siemens S7 PLCs driving centrifuges.
Mirai was an IoT DDoS botnet over the internet.
Industroyer spoke power-grid protocols in Ukraine.
Triton targeted a safety controller.

stem: Which port identifies Siemens S7comm traffic to a PLC?
explanation: Siemens S7 PLCs use ISO-TSAP on TCP 102; the Nmap s7-info script reads module and firmware details there.
optionNotes: 4840 is OPC UA.
502 is Modbus/TCP.
Correct: S7comm runs over ISO-TSAP on 102.

stem: EC-Council lists attacks on the RF remote controllers of cranes and industrial machines. Which of these is such an attack?
options: Injecting SQL into a plant database
Replaying a captured 'move' command to a crane's radio receiver
explanation: Industrial RF remotes can be vulnerable to replay, command injection, e-stop abuse and malicious reprogramming.
optionNotes: Phishing targets people, not the RF link.
SQL injection is a web/database attack.
Correct: capture-and-replay against the industrial radio link.
That is a wireless (Wi-Fi) attack, not an industrial RF remote attack.

stem: Why do defenders prefer passive monitoring over active scanning on OT networks?
options: Passive monitoring is the only method that finds any devices
Active scanning is illegal on all networks
Active scanning can crash fragile controllers and disrupt the process
explanation: Old OT devices can hang under scan traffic, so SP 800-82r3 favors passive monitoring and coordinated, windowed active checks.
optionNotes: Monitoring does not encrypt anything.
Active scanning also finds devices, but at higher risk.
Authorized active scanning is legal; the concern is operational risk.
Correct.

stem: During an authorized assessment a report line reads `502/tcp open modbus | modbus-discover: sid 0x64: Slave ID data: ...`. What has the script done?
options: Confirmed a Modbus server and read its slave ID / device identification
Uploaded new ladder logic to the PLC
explanation: The Nmap modbus-discover script (intrusive category) enumerates slave IDs and reads device identification on 502.
optionNotes: Correct: modbus-discover enumerates slave IDs and device info.
It does not write logic; it reads identification.
Modbus has no password to brute-force.
Classic Modbus is unencrypted, so there is nothing to decrypt.

stem: A blue team wants to build a picture of an OT network purely from captured traffic, without sending any packets to the devices. Which tool fits?
explanation: GRASSMARLIN and Zeek+ICSNPP analyze captured traffic to map assets and log ICS protocol commands without probing devices.
optionNotes: Hydra is an online password guesser.
Correct: GRASSMARLIN passively maps OT networks.
Metasploit is an active exploitation framework.
sqlmap is a SQL injection tool.

stem: An internet-facing PLC on a small water system still uses the vendor's out-of-the-box password, and a report shows it was reachable from a device-search engine. Which two ATT&CK for ICS ideas are in play?
options: Loss of Safety and Damage to Property
Internet Accessible Device and Default Credentials
explanation: Exposed PLCs with default passwords are a recurring entry point (for example the 2023 Unitronics defacements).
optionNotes: Those are impact effects, not the entry point.
Those are a component and a collection technique, not this exposure.
Correct.
Those need on-path access, not an exposed default login.

stem: In ATT&CK for ICS, what does Program Upload refer to?
options: Reading the control logic from a controller
Writing new logic to a controller
explanation: Upload reads logic from the controller (collection); Download writes logic to it (can change the process).
optionNotes: Correct: upload reads logic from the device.
That is Program Download.
That is Device Restart/Shutdown.
That is Network Sniffing.

stem: In ISA/IEC 62443, what is a zone?
options: The path that carries traffic between groups of assets
The achieved security level of a system
A group of assets that share the same security requirements
explanation: Zones group assets by risk and shared requirements; conduits connect zones and are secured as units.
optionNotes: That is a conduit.
That is a data diode.
That is SL-A.
Correct.

stem: A plant's business analysts need read-only access to production data, but the control network must stay protected. Which design best fits the Purdue model?
options: Put the PLCs on the corporate VLAN
Give analysts direct Modbus access to the PLCs
Replicate the historian into an industrial DMZ that business users read from
Expose the HMI to the internet with a password
explanation: The industrial DMZ lets business users reach a replicated historian without any path into the control zone; Level 4 must not reach Levels 0-2.
optionNotes: Flattening the network removes the protection.
Direct Level 4 to Level 1 access violates the model.
Correct: an industrial DMZ (Level 3.5) isolates control from business access.
Exposing the HMI is exactly what CISA warns against.

stem: Which NIST publication is the 2023 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security?
explanation: SP 800-82r3 renamed the scope from ICS to OT and provides an OT overlay of SP 800-53 controls.
optionNotes: SP 800-115 is the security testing guide.
Correct.
8259A is the IoT device baseline.
SP 800-53 is the general control catalog.

stem: After studying the Triton incident, a refinery wants to reduce the chance that malware can reach and reprogram its safety controllers. Which combination fits best?
options: Isolate the SIS on its own network and keep the controller key switch in RUN
Move the SIS onto the business VLAN for easier patching
Give the SIS a public IP for remote support
Share credentials between the SIS and the control system
explanation: Triton reached a safety controller over the network; isolation, a RUN key switch and program-change alarms are the lessons.
optionNotes: Correct.
Sharing a VLAN with business IT increases exposure.
A public IP is the opposite of isolation.
Shared credentials let one compromise spread.

stem: What does a data diode enforce that a firewall does not?
options: Traffic can physically flow in only one direction
Traffic is encrypted end to end
explanation: A data diode is one-way by physics; a firewall filters two-way traffic by rules that can be misconfigured.
optionNotes: It does not manage passwords.
Correct.
A diode does not itself encrypt traffic.
It is not an anti-malware product.

stem: Which CISA recommendation most directly reduces the risk of OT devices being found by internet device-search engines?
options: Remove OT connections from the public internet
explanation: CISA's first primary OT mitigation is to take OT off the public internet and reach it only through a VPN with phishing-resistant MFA.
optionNotes: Renaming tags does not hide an exposed device.
Storage size does not affect exposure.
Correct.
Email is unrelated to OT exposure.

stem: Which protocol lets IPv6 packets run over low-power IEEE 802.15.4 links?
explanation: 6LoWPAN compresses and adapts IPv6 for constrained 802.15.4 radios.
optionNotes: LoRaWAN is a separate LPWAN, not IPv6-over-802.15.4.
BACnet is a building-automation protocol.
MQTT is an application protocol.
Correct: RFC 4944.

stem: A wearable and its phone pair using BLE 'Just Works', and a review flags that the link can be intercepted by an on-path attacker. Why?
options: Just Works sends the PIN in the clear
Just Works provides no man-in-the-middle protection
Just Works disables all encryption permanently
explanation: BLE Just Works pairing is convenient but offers no MITM protection; Numeric Comparison, Passkey or OOB do.
optionNotes: There is no PIN entry in Just Works.
Correct.
It still derives a link key; the gap is MITM protection.
It is not certificate-based.

stem: Which framework is used specifically for testing IEEE 802.15.4 / Zigbee networks?
explanation: KillerBee is the go-to toolkit for Zigbee / 802.15.4 assessment.
optionNotes: sqlmap targets web SQL injection.
Ubertooth is for Bluetooth.
HackRF is a general SDR.
Correct.

stem: NISTIR 8259 groups six manufacturer activities. How are they split?
explanation: Four activities apply before sale (identify customers, research needs, address them, plan support) and two after sale (how and what to communicate).
optionNotes: Not the split used.
Not the split used.
Correct.
Not the split used.

stem: A manufacturer wants devices to accept only firmware it has signed and to refuse older, vulnerable versions. Which two properties are needed?
options: Shared keys and open debug ports
No update mechanism and manual flashing
explanation: OWASP I4 and NIST SP 800-193 call for authenticated firmware and rollback protection.
optionNotes: Correct: both are part of a secure update mechanism (OWASP I4).
Cleartext delivery is insecure.
Those weaken security.
That leaves devices unpatchable.

stem: Which device provides the operator's screen for watching and commanding an industrial process?
explanation: The HMI is the operator interface; compromising or falsifying it hides the true process state.
optionNotes: An RTU is a remote field unit.
A PLC runs the control logic.
A historian stores process data.
Correct: human-machine interface.

stem: A grid operator reviews malware that reused IEC 60870-5-104 in a 2022 attack, echoing an earlier 2016 substation incident. Which malware pair is this?
explanation: Industroyer2 (2022) reused IEC-104 against a Ukrainian substation, echoing Industroyer/CrashOverride in 2016.
optionNotes: Those are IoT DDoS botnets.
Those targeted Siemens PLCs / were espionage tools.
Correct: Industroyer (2016) and Industroyer2 (2022).
Triton and TRISIS are two names for the same safety-system malware.

stem: Which port is registered for DNP3?
explanation: DNP3 uses TCP/UDP 20000; its Secure Authentication extension adds challenge-response.
optionNotes: Correct.
502 is Modbus/TCP.
47808 is BACnet/IP.
4840 is OPC UA.

stem: Which ATT&CK for ICS technique describes finding a PLC or HMI that answers directly from the internet?
explanation: Internet Accessible Device (Nmap/Shodan reachability) is a common OT reconnaissance and entry finding.
optionNotes: Loss of View is an impact, not discovery.
Correct.
Program Download writes logic to a controller.
Sniffing captures traffic on a network.

stem: An authorized report shows `47808/udp open bacnet | bacnet-info: Vendor Name: ...; Firmware: ...`. Which service answered?
explanation: Port 47808/udp with bacnet-info output identifies a BACnet device and its vendor and firmware.
optionNotes: Modbus is 502.
Correct: bacnet-info queries UDP 47808.
OPC UA is 4840.

stem: How many foundational requirements (FRs) does ISA/IEC 62443 define?
explanation: The seven FRs: identification/authentication control, use control, system integrity, data confidentiality, restricted data flow, timely response, resource availability.
optionNotes: Not correct.
Four is the number of security levels, not FRs.
Correct: FR1 to FR7.
Not correct.

stem: A site wants to stop USB-borne malware from reaching engineering workstations, a lesson drawn from Stuxnet. Which controls fit best?
explanation: Stuxnet spread by USB; media control, allowlisting and verifying PLC logic are the lessons.
optionNotes: Disabling logging removes detection.
Public IPs increase exposure.
Shared logins spread compromise.
Correct.

stem: In the Purdue model, which boundary is commonly implemented as an industrial DMZ?
options: Between the business network (Level 4) and site operations (Level 3)
Between the HMI and its monitor
explanation: An industrial DMZ sits between IT (Level 4/5) and OT operations (Level 3) so business users never reach controllers directly.
optionNotes: Correct: the IT/OT boundary, sometimes called Level 3.5.
Not a DMZ boundary.
Not a network boundary.
Not a network boundary.

stem: In an MQTT topic filter, what does the `#` wildcard match?
options: Only the broker's own `$SYS` status topics
Exactly one topic level at that position
The current topic level and every level below it
Only messages the broker has stored as retained
explanation: In MQTT, `#` is the multi-level wildcard: `home/#` matches `home` and everything under it. `+` matches exactly one level. This is why an anonymous broker that allows a subscription to `#` leaks every topic.
optionNotes: Wildcards at the first level do not match topics that start with `$`, such as `$SYS`.
That is the single-level wildcard `+`.
Correct: `#` is the multi-level wildcard and must be the last character of the filter.
Retained messages are a separate feature, not what a wildcard selects.

stem: A review of a smart camera finds that its cloud API returns another customer's video stream when the camera ID in the request is changed. Which OWASP IoT Top 10 (2018) category fits best?
explanation: OWASP I3 covers the web, cloud, API and mobile interfaces around the device. A cloud API without proper authorization checks is the classic I3 finding.
optionNotes: Correct: the flaw is in the cloud API around the device (I3).
I2 is about services running on the device itself, such as Telnet or UPnP.
I10 is about opening the device or reaching its debug ports.
I8 is about inventory, monitoring and decommissioning of devices.

stem: During a teardown, a product-security team finds a header on the circuit board that gives a root console over UART with no password. Which OWASP IoT Top 10 (2018) category does this finding belong to?
explanation: OWASP I10 covers physical access weaknesses: easy disassembly and exposed debug interfaces such as UART or JTAG. OWASP ISTG lists these physical interfaces as test targets.
optionNotes: I3 is about cloud, web, API and mobile interfaces around the device.
Correct: an open UART console is an I10 finding.
I7 is about cleartext traffic or secrets stored unprotected.
I4 is about unsigned or unverified firmware updates.

stem: A firewall review finds UDP 5683 open to the internet on a batch of field sensors. Which protocol is exposed, and what abuse does its RFC warn about?
options: Modbus/TCP, which accepts unauthenticated register writes
MQTT, which lets anonymous clients subscribe to every topic
UPnP/SSDP, which lets devices open router ports unasked
CoAP, which RFC 7252 warns can be abused for amplification
explanation: UDP 5683 is the default CoAP port (5684 for CoAP over DTLS). RFC 7252 section 11.3 warns that CoAP responses can be larger than requests, so an exposed endpoint can be used in amplification attacks.
optionNotes: Modbus/TCP uses TCP 502.
MQTT uses TCP 1883 (8883 with TLS), not UDP 5683.
SSDP uses UDP 1900.
Correct: CoAP on UDP 5683; RFC 7252 §11.3 covers amplification.

stem: A wireless sensor mesh suddenly lists dozens of "new" nodes that all share one radio fingerprint and try to join the routing. Which attack class fits best?
explanation: In a Sybil attack one physical node claims many identities to gain influence over the network, for example over routing or voting. Node authentication is the countermeasure.
optionNotes: Side-channel attacks leak secrets through power, timing or EM and need physical access.
Jamming floods the channel with noise; devices go offline instead of multiplying.
Replay resends one captured valid message; it does not create new identities.
Correct: one entity posing as many nodes.

stem: In EC-Council's five-phase IoT hacking methodology, which phase comes right after information gathering?
explanation: EC-Council's order is information gathering, vulnerability scanning, launch attacks, gain remote access, maintain access. Defenders run the first two against their own devices first.
optionNotes: Gaining remote access is the fourth phase.
Launching attacks is the third phase.
Correct: the second phase.
Maintaining access is the last phase.

stem: Which open-source hardware tool is built to monitor Bluetooth traffic, including Bluetooth Low Energy, during an authorized device assessment?
explanation: Ubertooth One is an open 2.4 GHz platform for Bluetooth monitoring and experimentation. KillerBee targets IEEE 802.15.4 / Zigbee instead.
optionNotes: KillerBee is the IEEE 802.15.4 / Zigbee framework.
Correct: Bluetooth monitoring platform.
JTAGulator finds JTAG and UART pins on a circuit board.
binwalk analyzes firmware images, not radio traffic.

stem: A hardware reviewer must find out which pins on an unfamiliar circuit board expose a JTAG or UART debug interface. Which tool is designed for this?
explanation: JTAGulator identifies on-chip debug interfaces (JTAG, UART) from unknown test points. Finding them lets the manufacturer confirm debug ports are disabled before shipping (OWASP I10).
optionNotes: Correct: it locates JTAG/UART pinouts.
ChipWhisperer is for side-channel power analysis and fault injection.
HackRF One is a software-defined radio.
GNU Radio is a signal-processing framework for radio work.

stem: An authorized scan report shows `1883/tcp open mqtt | mqtt-subscribe: Topics and their most recent payloads: $SYS/broker/version: ...`. What should the defender conclude?
options: The broker is a CoAP server answering resource discovery
The broker only accepts clients over TLS on this port
The broker let a client connect and subscribe without credentials
The broker rejected the script and returned an error banner
explanation: The mqtt-subscribe script connects to the broker and subscribes to topics; printing `$SYS` topics and payloads means the connection was accepted. Fix: disable anonymous access, add password files and ACLs, and move clients to TLS on 8883.
optionNotes: CoAP uses UDP 5683 and a different script (coap-resources).
1883 is the plaintext MQTT port; TLS is normally on 8883.
Correct: payloads were read, so anonymous access worked.
A rejected connection would not print topics and payloads.

stem: binwalk run on a camera's firmware image reports `Squashfs filesystem, little endian` at an offset. What does this tell the product-security team?
options: The image holds an unencrypted file system they can extract and review
The image is encrypted, so its contents cannot be inspected
The image carries a valid vendor signature and is trusted
The camera has a network service listening on that offset
explanation: binwalk identifies embedded file systems and compressed data. A readable Squashfs file system can be extracted and checked for hardcoded passwords, keys and outdated components (OWASP I1, I5).
optionNotes: Correct: extract it and look for secrets and old libraries.
An encrypted image would show high entropy, not a recognized file system.
binwalk signatures describe file formats, not code-signing status.
An offset is a position in the file, not a network port.

stem: Which OWASP project is a deliberately insecure firmware image built for practicing IoT security testing?
explanation: OWASP IoTGoat is intentionally vulnerable firmware for practice. ISVS is the verification standard, ISTG the testing guide and FSTM the firmware testing methodology.
optionNotes: FSTM is the Firmware Security Testing Methodology.
ISVS is a set of security requirements to verify against.
ISTG is the IoT Security Testing Guide.
Correct: deliberately vulnerable firmware.

stem: An office DVR was part of a Mirai botnet. IT rebooted it and plugged it straight back in, and it was reinfected within minutes. What step did they miss?
options: Running a full antivirus scan on the DVR's storage
Changing the default password before reconnecting it
Restoring the DVR's previous configuration backup
Moving the DVR to a new public IP address
explanation: Mirai lives in memory, so a reboot removes it, but the device stays exposed while the default password works. CISA's advice: reboot while disconnected, change the password to a strong one, and only then reconnect.
optionNotes: Mirai does not persist on storage; a reboot already clears it.
Correct: the weakness is the default password, not the infection.
A backup would restore the same default credentials.
Mirai scans the internet, so a new address is found again quickly.

stem: Which NISTIR 8259A capability lets a device report on its own security state, for example through logs that reveal it may have been compromised?
explanation: The 8259A core baseline has six capabilities: device identification, device configuration, data protection, logical access to interfaces, software update and cybersecurity state awareness. The last one covers reporting the device's state so compromise can be detected.
optionNotes: Correct: it supports detecting compromise.
Configuration is about changing the device's settings securely.
Logical access is about restricting who and what can use the interfaces.
Data protection covers keeping stored and sent data safe.

stem: Which NIST publication sets out the non-technical support manufacturers should give IoT customers, such as documentation and education?
explanation: NISTIR 8259B is the non-technical supporting capability core baseline (documentation, information and query reception, information dissemination, education and awareness). 8259A covers the technical device capabilities.
optionNotes: SP 800-193 is about platform firmware resiliency.
8259A lists the technical capabilities built into the device.
Correct: the non-technical baseline.
SP 800-82r3 is the guide to OT security.

stem: Smart TVs and badge readers share a flat network with staff laptops and file servers. Which change best limits the damage if one of these IoT devices is compromised?
options: Enable UPnP so each device opens only the ports it asks for
Put them on a separate segment that only allows the flows they need
Install endpoint antivirus agents on every IoT device
Give all IoT devices one shared, strong admin password
explanation: Segmentation (a separate VLAN or SSID with allowlisted flows) keeps a compromised device away from the rest of the network. ENISA calls this risk segmentation, and RFC 8520 MUD automates the allowlist.
optionNotes: UPnP lets devices open ports without review; CISA advises disabling it.
Correct: isolate and allow only what the device needs.
Most IoT devices cannot run endpoint agents.
A shared password means one leak unlocks every device.

stem: A vendor wants its boot firmware to block unauthorized changes, notice when the image is corrupted and restore a known-good copy. Which NIST publication frames firmware security around exactly these goals?
explanation: NIST SP 800-193 (Platform Firmware Resiliency Guidelines) is built on three principles: protect firmware from unauthorized change, detect corruption, and recover to a known-good state.
optionNotes: 8259A lists device capabilities such as software update, not the firmware resiliency model.
SP 800-213 guides federal agencies in setting IoT device requirements.
SP 800-82r3 is the guide to OT security.
Correct: platform firmware resiliency rests on protect, detect and recover.
